column3: Make the trace accept loop accept-and-spawn only
column11: Make the trace accept loop accept-and-spawn only.
column12: The trace2 accept loop did per-connection work inline before handing the connection to its reader thread: SO_RCVBUF setup, ingress bookkeeping, and a bootstrap read of up to 8 JSON lines under a 100ms recv timeout. This serialized all accepts behind each connection's bootstrap (one silent peer cost 100ms of accept time; a failed set_recv_timeout - macOS returns EINVAL from setsockopt when the peer has already shut down - silently removed the timeout entirely and let a single quiet connection wedge the accept loop forever). Git writes trace2 synchronously, so a wedged or slow accept loop blocks every traced git process in write() once the listen backlog and socket buffers fill (macOS: ~128 backlog, 8 KiB default buffers). Issue: https://github.com/git-ai-project/git-ai/issues/2157

column3: Drop unconsumed trace2 frames at ingestion
column11: Drop unconsumed trace2 frames at ingestion.
column12: Only six trace2 event types (start, def_repo, cmd_name, def_param, exit, atexit) are ever consumed downstream - the normalizer's dispatch discards everything else in its default arm. Yet the trace readers enqueued every frame of a mutating root, so the large majority of what a git process emits (version, cmd_path, cmd_ancestry, child/region/data/thread events, ...) traveled through JSON parsing, ingress bookkeeping, sequence allocation, and an ingest-queue slot only to be thrown away by the serial worker. Roughly 25-35 frames per commit, ~6 useful: the 16,384-slot queue effectively held only ~500 in-flight commits, which is exactly where a 512-commit burst against a busy worker tipped into fail-closed attribution loss.

column11: Replace dirty-bucket tracking with session-bucket reconciliation.

column12: - Global cross-session dedup (schema v2 global indexes): claude   --resume/--continue/fork copies the parent conversation into a new   session file with the original message/request ids, and session-   scoped dedup re-counted the whole history on every resume. column12: Daemon resources: - Sweeps prefilter with one stat per session compared against the token   database's size/mtime snapshot, so unchanged sessions cost no   spawn_blocking, DB reads, or repo discovery; repo discovery (gix   config parse) is deferred until events are actually emitted; the   30-minute ticker skips missed ticks after suspend instead of   replaying them. - Emission reconciles the session in one grouped query (changed_buckets)   instead of ~2N per-bucket queries per pass. - Per-file error backoff (5s/30s/5m/30m via processing_errors +   last_error_at): a permanently failing transcript is no longer re-read   to the poison point on every trigger. - Backfill applies the retention cutoff at extraction, so first-run   backfill does not insert and upload months of pre-cutoff buckets that   the next prune would delete.

column3: Accuracy-review fixes for the worker: read robustness, revisions, blame
column11: Accuracy-review fixes for the worker: read robustness, revisions, blame.
column12: Behavioral fixes: - Byte-level lossy line reads: a single invalid-UTF-8 byte previously   made every pass error at the same committed offset forever (backoff   or not), losing all usage after that point; the bad line now decodes   lossily, fails JSON parsing, is skipped, and the cursor advances -   matching upstream ccusage's byte reads. - A final line without a trailing newline that already parses as   complete JSON is counted (an agent killed between the object and its   newline never grows the file again, and the size/mtime snapshot would   have suppressed it forever); genuinely half-written JSON still stays   pending. - Unreadable persisted extractor state (corrupt or cross-version) now   resets the read cursor along with the state: continuing mid-file on   default codex state would book the session's entire cumulative   history as one fresh delta. The full re-read is idempotent via   entry-identity dedup. - Emission revisions are floored to wall-clock seconds, so deleting the   token DB (flag off) and re-enabling can never restart revisions below   values the server already holds under the highest-revision upsert. - Cross-session reconcile failures are no longer charged to the   triggering task's healthy transcript (which was pushed into error   backoff with misleading diagnostics); the durable flags retry them.

column3: fix(daemon): never run family side effects inline on the trace ingest worker
column11: Never run family side effects inline on the trace ingest worker.
column12: A long write-op side-effect pass (e.g. a large checkout/commit in a monorepo) used to execute inline on the serial trace-ingest worker: apply_trace_payload_to_state took the family exec lock and drained the family sequencer in place, and the non-sequencer Applied branch ran maybe_apply_side_effects_for_applied_command directly. While one family ground through minutes of git work, the processed_trace_ingest_seq watermark froze, so checkpoint admission (which waits on that watermark) stalled for every repository family: checkpoints were "received into bounded ingress" but never admitted, queued trace payloads backed up, and the socket health check tripped processing_stalled restarts that were deferred while the very checkpoints the stall blocked remained outstanding (#2252). Issue: https://github.com/git-ai-project/git-ai/issues/2252

column3: test(daemon): bound the family causal fence with a grace window
column11: Bound the family causal fence with a grace window.
column12: A completed sequencer entry, a sync, or an await must wait for an older open mutating trace root only while that root may have changed refs with frames still in flight: a root whose final frame is queued holds until the worker catches up; other roots hold for one causal grace, after which a root whose git process is provably alive and has written nothing is a still-running interactive command and is released (once, logged), a root seen starting a post-write hook has already changed refs and holds until it finishes, and a root whose process is gone holds until a hard cap. Shared harness helpers replace the duplicated raw traced-git wiring and synthetic open roots, and a blocked-hook git helper exercises pre- and post-write hooks for real.

column11: Source tokens and cost from TokenUsage events exclusively.
column12: git-ai usage previously re-parsed raw transcript JSON embedded in SessionEvents (per-message Claude usage, cumulative codex totals) and priced it with a flat "rough display estimate".
